question: What law gives the Strahler numbers (untangling phases) of layered random monotone circuits: the infinite-width recursion Q_{L+1} = Q_L - q_L^2/2 to depth 10^5 against the Burgers asymptotics, and exact finite-width simulations?

definitions.circuit: width w, depth d, inputs true w.p. 1/2, each gate AND or OR w.p. 1/2 reading two distinct gates of the layer below
definitions.rank: least Strahler number of a derivation (OR: least max(rank,1) over true inputs; AND: max, +1 on ties)

public_inputs.run: scripts/longrun.py launch on job.py; summarize.py RUN

forbidden_inputs: Changing settings, seeds, readings, predictions or decision rules after seeing registered results
primary_observable: Predictions G, M1-M7, S1-S3 of research/LAYER-RANK-20261117-001/preregistration.md, evaluated by summarize.py.
cheapest_meaningful_control: The finite-width simulations against the infinite-width recursion (S1).

predictions.M7: slope of mean + ln(L)/4 vs sqrt(L) in [0.64, 0.69]
predictions.S1: simulation within 5% of the recursion at d <= w/128
predictions.S3: c = sqrt(w) x slope over 40w..100w in [0.3, 1.5] for w = 64..1024, max/min <= 1.5

decision_rules.each prediction: holds or fails as stated in the pre-registration

stop_rule: One run and its read-out; referee hand-off; report.
runtime: A few minutes on three workers.
